questions.q: What is the real, answerable compliance question this lesson centers on?
options: Who accessed this data, when, and were they authorized to at that time
How many total rows exist in a given table
Which cloud region a table's files are physically stored in
How much a cluster costs per hour to run
questions.explain: A real compliance requirement is almost always one specific, answerable query someone can actually run — not a policy document.

questions.q: Why can't audit logs alone answer whether access to sensitive data was authorized?
options: Audit logs record who ran a query and when, but not whether that access was actually entitled at that time
Audit logs don't exist in Unity Catalog
Audit logs only record failed queries, never successful ones
Audit logs are deleted automatically after 24 hours
questions.explain: Activity and authorization are two different questions — audit logs answer the first, not the second, on their own.

questions.q: Why does lineage alone fail to answer 'who actually saw this sensitive data'?
options: Lineage traces what downstream tables/dashboards a source feeds, but doesn't record who actually queried it
Lineage only tracks tables created in the last 24 hours
Lineage is only available for row filters, not column masks
Lineage automatically masks all sensitive columns
questions.explain: Lineage answers exposure risk (what's downstream), not activity (who actually ran a query against it).

questions.q: In the worked example about an unmasked SSN in Q3, why is checking today's masking policy not sufficient?
options: The masking policy that was actually active at the time of each historical query might differ from what's active today
Masking policies are recalculated every time a query runs, regardless of history
Today's policy is always identical to every past policy by design
Masking policies cannot change once created
questions.explain: A policy could have changed mid-quarter — answering the question requires the access-control state in effect at each query's own timestamp.

questions.q: What do compliance frameworks like GDPR, HIPAA, and SOC 2 add on top of the technical backbone this lesson describes?
options: Retention periods, response obligations, and requirements for who must be able to answer which question, by when
An entirely separate technical mechanism unrelated to audit logs, lineage, or access control
A requirement to disable Unity Catalog entirely
A mandate to use only Databricks-backed secret scopes
questions.explain: Frameworks layer obligations on top of the same underlying question — none of them invent a new technical mechanism to answer it.
